title: What if my gifts are just noise?
keyTakeaway: Speech without love is just noise — a clanging cymbal. Love is the more excellent way.
scriptureText: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.
keywords: speak love noise cymbal gong tongues angels gifts paul excellent way 1 corinthians 13
answer: Without love, even speaking in the languages of men and angels is just noise — a clanging cymbal.
why: Pastor Kincer explains Paul’s picture: a cymbal clanging by itself would drive you nuts in about 30 seconds. He says love is more important than both kinds of languages — men’s and angels’.

quotes.text: Though or if I speak with tongues of men and angels, but have not love, I am become a sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.
And if I had someone over there just clang the cymbals together, you know, in about 30 seconds, you would go, “You’re driving me nuts. What’s the point?”
There’s languages of men, like they spoke on the day of Pentecost. And there are languages of angels. But the key is love is more important than both of those.

title: Can I serve God and still miss knowing Him?
keyTakeaway: Being used by God is not the same as being known by Him; gifts without love still hear “I never knew you.”
scriptureText: Many will say to Me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in Your name, cast out demons in Your name, and done many wonders in Your name?’ And then I will declare to them, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you who practice lawlessness!’
keywords: matthew 7:22 7:23 i never knew you gifts without love prophesy cast out demons mighty works known by god 1 corinthians 13:2
answer: Yes. You can be used by God — even prophesy and do mighty works in Jesus’ name — and still miss the most important thing: love.
why: Pastor Kincer points to Jesus’ warning about people who prophesied and cast out demons in His name, yet hear “I never knew you.” He says they were used by God but missed love, which he describes as obeying God.

quotes.text: See, love is to obey God. And he had the message, but he didn’t have the love.

See, they had faith to do all these things and these gifts and these spiritual manifestations were working in them. And Jesus said, “I will say to them, I never knew you.” Depart from me, you workers of iniquity.
You see, you didn’t have love. You might have been used of God to do things, but you missed the important thing, and that is love.

title: Does real love insist on its own way?
keyTakeaway: Love … does not seek its own, … thinks no evil.
scriptureText: Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil; does not rejoice in iniquity, but rejoices in the truth; bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
tags: love does not demand its own way
keywords: 1 corinthians 13:4 13:5 13:6 13:7 love patient kind own way record of wrongs not easily provoked biblical love
answer: No. Real love doesn’t demand its own way. It wants the right way — the truth.
why: Pastor Kincer walks through Paul’s description of love: patient, kind, not proud or rude. Love doesn’t demand its own way in the family, the church or the community, and it keeps no record of wrongs.

quotes.text: Love does not seek its own way. Well, it’s going to be my way. I’m going to hit the highway. You know, love doesn’t demand its own way in the family, in the church, or in the community. It demands the right way, the truth.
Love is not easily provoked. It, you know, they’re not touchy. You know, if you don’t say the right thing or do the right thing, they’re all ticked off. And love doesn’t do that.

title: Is God looking for fruit — or fireworks?
keyTakeaway: Character (love) comes before chasing spiritual fireworks.
scriptureText: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace… God is love. Love never fails.
keywords: galatians 5:22 fruit of the spirit love first 1 john 4:8 god is love manifestations character 1 corinthians 13:8 love never fails
answer: Fruit comes first. Love is the first fruit of the Spirit and the peak of God’s character, and you can’t have the manifestations of the Spirit without it.
why: Pastor Kincer notes that love is listed first among the fruit of the Spirit, that God is love, and that love sits at the top of sharing in the divine nature. His point: the fruit and character of God come before the manifestations.

quotes.text: Love, joy, peace. It’s the first fruit. 1 John 4:8 says, “God is love.” See, that is exactly what God is. He just gave us the description of God.

So the love is at the peak of divine character and it’s at the beginning of the fruits of the spirit. And believe me, Paul is telling us, you can’t have the manifestations of the spirit without the fruit and the divine character of God. That’s what he’s telling us. This is the way to get it.

title: Does “be perfect” mean never fail?
keyTakeaway: “Be perfect” means grow into maturity — not never mess up.
scriptureText: Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect. … that you may be perfect and complete, lacking nothing.
keywords: matthew 5:48 be perfect mature james 1:4 perfect entire lacking nothing spiritual maturity completeness hebrews 5:14
answer: No. Pastor Kincer says “be perfect” means spiritual maturity and completeness, not a life with no flaws.
why: Pastor Kincer says people hear “be perfect” and think it means never sinning. He points to Hebrews 5:14 and James 1:4 to show it is about growing up and being complete, lacking nothing.

quotes.text: “Be you therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” This is Jesus talking.
And they thought perfect was just living a life that had no flaws in it. No, it’s coming to what? Spiritual maturity, spiritual completeness.
Let patience have her perfect work, that you may be what? Perfect and entire, lacking what? Nothing.

title: What is the real goal of God’s Word?
keyTakeaway: Worship, prayer, and gifts are means — love from a pure heart is the goal.
scriptureText: Now the purpose of the commandment is love from a pure heart, from a good conscience, and from sincere faith.

answer: Love from a pure heart. Paul says that is the goal of the commandment.
why: Pastor Kincer says “end” in this verse means goal. We tend to think the goal is eternal life or the gifts of the Spirit, he says, but it is love.

quotes.text: Now the end of the commandment is love out of a pure heart. The word end means the goal. You see the goal of the word of God is love out of a pure heart.
See, we think it’s eternal life. No, you’re going to live eternally no matter what.
We think that it’s the gifts of the spirit in our circles.
And it’s not. It’s love. And that’s why we have such phoniness in the spirit-filled world as we try to push something that God isn’t doing.

title: Do we want God’s blessings — or His rule?

quotes.text: God said to Samuel, they have rejected me that I should not rule over them. They haven’t rejected you, Samuel. They rejected me.

See, the people didn’t want God telling them what to do. Is that America? Yeah, we want to go to heaven. You see, we want his blessings. We want him to prosper us, but we don’t want to do what he tells us to do.
People want God’s blessings and God’s approval. But God wants to rule in their life. He wants the Scriptures to rule in their life, and they don’t want it.

quotes.text: There’s many groups doing what’s right in their own eyes, hiring and appointing ministers to flatter them, to please them, not God, as it says in Isaiah 30:10, speak to us smooth things, speak to us deceit, don’t speak to us right things.
We don’t want to hear about good works, we don’t want to hear about what’s right, we want to hear that we’re okay.
And so they get the money, they get the big fancy houses, they get the cars, they get the fame, they pay ministers to preach what they want to hear.

title: What if a nation turns back to God?

You speak the word and the word convicts and convinces people. The word does it. You don’t have to force them.
